title: The Isolated Queen's Pawn
subtitle: A permanent weakness that attacks — and how to defuse it.
goals: Play the IQP for activity and the d5 break
Blockade the pawn as the defender
Know which side wants to trade pieces

steps.say: The pawn on d4 has no friends on the c- or e-files: it is ISOLATED, and it can never be defended by another pawn. That makes it a long-term weakness — and a short-term weapon. It grants space, two open files for the rooks, and the e5 and c5 squares for pieces. The whole struggle has one rule: **the attacker wants pieces on the board; the defender wants them traded off.** Every trade brings the endgame, where the isolani is simply weak.

steps.prompt: You have the isolani. Play the thematic break that turns weakness into attack!
hints: The isolated pawn's dream is to advance: d4–d5 opens lines for both bishops and the rooks while the pawn is still alive.
d5! Open the position while you have the more active pieces.

line.say: The thematic break. The pawn stops being a target by advancing at the perfect moment — lines open for the c4 bishop and the d-file rook, and Black's position creaks. The rule: an isolani that pushes is an asset; an isolani that sits is a liability.

rejections.say: A sensible developing move, but it invites trades — and every trade helps the DEFENDER. With an isolated pawn you must play for the break and the attack before the endgame arrives.
Reasonable, yet slow: Black consolidates with ...Nb4 and ...Nfd5, blockading the pawn permanently. The break d5 is available right now, and its moment does not come twice.

steps.wrongSay: The isolani wants to advance while your pieces are the more active ones. Which pawn break?
steps.successSay: Push it or lose it: the isolated pawn is a weapon with a short fuse.

steps.prompt: Now defend against it. Start the blockade — the square in front of the pawn is everything!
hints: The defender's method: put a piece on d5, where no pawn can ever chase it, and the isolani is frozen forever.
Nb4 heads for d5 — the blockading square.

line.say: The knight begins its journey to d5. Once a knight lands there the pawn can never advance, White's attack has no fuel, and the endgame — where the isolani is just weak — comes closer with every trade. Blockade first, win the pawn later.

rejections.say: A useful move eventually, but it does nothing about the pawn's advance. Against an isolani the first job is always the BLOCKADE: control d5 before White can play it.
This opens the position for White's pieces — exactly what the isolani player wants. The defender keeps things closed and trades pieces, not pawns.

steps.wrongSay: Aim a piece at the square directly in front of the isolated pawn.
steps.successSay: Blockade, trade, then win the pawn — the three-step defence against every isolani.

steps.say: Carry these away: with an isolani, keep pieces on, aim at the kingside, and look for d4–d5 at every moment. Against one, blockade d5 with a knight, trade every pair of pieces you can, and head for an endgame where you simply win the pawn. Both plans are correct — the position just asks which side of it you're on.
